user_input: How to find the last columns of a pandas dataframe
model_output:
You can use the `iloc` property of a Pandas DataFrame to access specific rows and columns. To find the last column of a DataFrame, you can use the following syntax:
```css
df.iloc[:, -1]
```
This will return the last column of the DataFrame, which is the column with the lowest index number. You can also use negative indexing to access previous columns, so if you want to access the second-to-last column, you would use:
```css
df.iloc[:, -2]
```
This syntax works for any DataFrame, regardless of its shape or size. If you want to select a specific range of rows and columns, you can use the `iloc` property with a list of row indices and a slice of column indices. For example:
```csharp
df.iloc[0:5, 0:3]
```
This will return the first 5 rows and the first 3 columns of the DataFrame.
